_comment: Mutants that survive for a reason somebody established, so that a run's
output can be read as 'what changed' rather than 'what is there'.
An entry is a claim that this specific change cannot be observed. Do not
add one on inspection alone: apply the mutation by hand, watch the suite
stay green, and say in `reason` what makes it unobservable. A mutant that
is merely untested is not equivalent -- it is a missing test.
And a green suite only proves equivalence over the inputs the fixtures
reach. A sibling repository nearly filed `make([]T, 0, len(a)+len(b))` with
`+` mutated to `-` as equivalent -- capacity is only a hint, the reasoning
is sound -- until `len(b) > len(a)` makes the capacity negative and panics.
Their fixture had both lengths at 1, so the suite stayed green and said
nothing. So the question is not whether the reasoning is right but over
which inputs it holds, and whether the fixtures go there.
Everything not listed here is reported as new. That is accurate rather
than noisy: the classifications made in earlier rounds live in tp closure
reasons, which is exactly the place a later round cannot read them from.
Moving one here is what makes it durable.

survivors.reason: NextID keeps the highest id seen, so `n > highest` and `n >= highest` assign the same value: on equality the assignment writes back what is already held. Verified by hand on 2026-09-01 -- applied `>=`, `go test ./internal/finding` stayed green. The comment above the line says the same thing, and it predates this file.

rank cuts the qualified list with `qualified = qualified[:limit]`, and `>` against `>=` differs only when len(qualified) == limit, where the cut is `s = s[:len(s)]`: same length, same elements, and only the elements are copied out after it. limit is max(MaxCandidates, 0), so no negative bound reaches the slice. Verified by hand on 2026-09-11 -- applied `>=`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/reinvention` stayed green. The fixtures reach len < limit (4 against 5) and len > limit (4 against 3, 1 against 0 and -1) but not len == limit; that case is the identity reslice above, which the language fixes rather than a fixture.

Comment.String allocates `make([]string, 0, len(ownedRegions)+1)`, and `-1` changes only the capacity hint from 4 to 2: append grows the slice and the joined text is identical. The operand is not an input: ownedRegions is an unexported package var holding exactly the three owned regions of §8.1.3 and nothing appends to it, so the capacity is 2 on every call and never reaches the negative value that panics `make`. Verified by hand on 2026-09-11 -- applied `-1`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/render/` and `./internal/draft/` stayed green.

withoutRegion computes `length := strings.Index(text[start:], region.close)` where text[start:] begins with region.open, and `< 0` against `<= 0` differs only when length == 0, i.e. when the close marker matches at the very position the open marker starts. No input reaches that: each pair is `<!-- cr:NAME -->` against `<!-- cr:/NAME -->`, which differ at byte 8 ('/' against the name's first letter), inside both markers, so a string opening with one cannot open with the other. Verified by hand on 2026-09-11 -- applied `<= 0`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/render/` and `./internal/draft/` stayed green. The equivalence rests on that byte: a future region whose close marker is a prefix of its open marker would make the mutant observable.

NOT equivalent -- unobservable, and entered as such. The guard is `released := held.Unlock(); err == nil && released != nil`, and the mutant `err != nil` differs only when Unlock itself fails: then the original reports the release error after a good write and keeps the write error after a bad one, while the mutant does the reverse. gofrs/flock v0.13.0 returns an error from Unlock only when flock(LOCK_UN) fails on a descriptor it holds open and locked, and held is a local with no seam to inject that. Verified by hand on 2026-09-11 -- applied `err != nil`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/state` stayed green. Reaching it needs a seam in a closed task's production code for an error path the lock does not produce in practice; not worth that change. Revisit if the ledger's lock ever gains an injectable interface.
